 JUDGMENT Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100355010/
1
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 07.01.2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 07.01.2023 at about 6.00 a.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51- AB-7922 as a loader and unloader, while proceeding so reached near Madapura Gate, BM road, Ramanagara Taluk & District, at that time the Ashok Leyland vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-30-BP-7120 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and suddenly took his vehicle to the right side of the road and dashed against the vehicle in which petitioner was traveling.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Sai Krupa Hospital, Kumbalagodu,
Bengaluru wherein he underwent surgery and later he was shifted to Kozhikode District Co-Operative Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent one more surgery and he has spent more than Rs.8,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as a Loader and Unloader and he was earning a sum of Rs.900/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his psychical work or lead a normal life as he was doing prior to the said accident and thereby he has suffer permanent loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 remained absent hence, placed exparte.

Respondent No.2- Insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement admitting the issuance of policy and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

The accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the petitioner's vehicle as he did not maintain distance, drive the same at high speed and tried to overtake the alleged lorry from left and he himself dashed and caused the accident
, as such the petition is not maintainable for one's own negligence.
Hence this is clear case of Volunti non fit injuria.
Further denied the occurrence, mode and involvement of the alleged Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-30-BP-7120.
Further contended the non-compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous in- juries due to the actionable negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-30- BP-7120 by its driver,
in RTA took place on 07.01.2023 at about 6.00 a.m., near Madapura Gate, BM Road, Ramanagara Taluk & District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Further, two witnesses have examined as PW.2 and 3, through them got marked documents at Ex.P.12 to 15.
Inspite of given sufficient opportunity the respondent No.2 did not adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders

for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:

ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, wound certificate, IMV report and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Sudhin T. the driver of the Canter in which the petitioner was traveling.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar along with rough sketch was prepared by the I.O.
As per the said spot mahazar and sketch the accident is in the right portion of the road.
The Ex.P.5 is the IMV report wherein the offending lorry has got damaged in its rear right side and the canter in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damaged in its front and left side.

This the contents of the Ex.P.5 IMV report along with Ex.P.3 spot mahazar shows that the offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120 vehicle to its right side suddenly and thereby it got dashed the right side going tanker in which the petitioner was traveling.

The contents of mahazar and rough skeetch helped the petitioner to prove his case and alleged negligence of offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120.
10.

The Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company vehemently argued that the as the accident is in the right side of the road, the driver of the canter in which petitioner was traveling Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100355010/
3 also contributed towards the cause of the accident.
As such prays to consider the contributory negligence.

But on perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar and rough sketch along with Ex.P5 IMV report, the canter of the petitioner was proceeding in the straight right side road and the driver of offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120 has came to its right side.
The driver of the offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120 is not examined before this court to show that he has given prior indications before coming to right side of the road.
On other hand the petitioner examined the driver of Canter bearing No.KA-51-AB-7922 as PW.3 who deposed about the negligence of driver of offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120.
The respondents have not lead any evidence in support of their defence.

11. Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP- 7120, and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP- 7120.

No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12.
The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending lorry bearing No.TN- 30-BP-7120.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120.
13.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.

The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner or the driver of the canter in which the petitioner was traveling for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of offending lorry bearing No.TN-30-BP-7120 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

15. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by the negligence of the driver of the canter, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.

16. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar along with rough sketch and Ex.P5 IMV report falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence of the driver of the canter for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 6 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 07.01.2023 which is caused by the driver of the Ashok Leyland vehicle bearing No.TN- 30-BP-7120 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 40 years.
But he has not produced any age proof.

In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to Sai Krupa Hospital, Kumbalagodu, Bengaluru wherein he underwent surgery and later he was shifted to Kozhikode District Co- Operative Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent one more surgery.

entities.text: Kozhikode District Co- Operative Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 & 10 the petitioner sustained fracture of both arm left, fracture medial condyle tibia, degloving injury of foot left side and right Olecranon fracture and he underwent surgeries.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.95,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100355010/
5 b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P8 and 11, amounting to Rs.3,52,483/- and Rs.94,942/- respectively.
These bills are not seriously disputed.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.4,47,500/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working as a Loader and unloader earning Rs.900/- per day.
In this regard petitioner has not produced any documents.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P7 & 10 the petitioner was admitted to Sai Krupa Hospital and The Kozhikode District Co-Operative Hospital for 13 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total three months period including 13 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 3 months =
Rs.48,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru as PW.2, through him clinical notes and x-ray which are marked at Ex.P.12 and 13.

entities.text: Sai Ortho and Dental Center, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained left forearm both bones fracture, left medial condyle tibia fracture degloving injury left foot with right olecranon fracture and he underwent surgery ORIF with plate and screw for the left radius ulna, ORIF with plate and screw for the left proximal tibia, wound debridement and suturing for the left foot and conservative management for the right elbow and later got discharged on 10.01.2023.
Again he admitted to The Kozhikode District Co-Operative Hospital on 11.01.2023 and underwent ORIF for the AC joint dislocation with end button on 13.01.2023 and later discharged on 19.01.2023.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 51%, left upper limb at 39% and of whole body at 27%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
No other expert evidence is adduced by the respondents.
According to the petitioner he was working as Loader and Unloader.
The alleged injuries and the evidence of the PW.2 doctor reveals that the petitioner cannot do physical work.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7 both the hands and left leg has got major injuries.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 25% to the whole body.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his age.
As per the medical records and discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7 and P10 the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 37 and 36 years.
In his affidavit filed for examination in chief the petitioner has stated that he is aged about 37 years.
The proper multiplier for the age group 35-40 is 15.
By considering the same the age of the petitioner is considered as 37 years.

Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100355010/
6

entities.text: Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15X 25% =Rs.7,20,000/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P7 & 10 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 13 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 13 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.13,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 13 days in the hospital.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
Towards future medical expenses: The PW.2 doctor stated that the petitioner need another surgery for the removal of the implants which may estimate around Rs.90,000/-.
By considering the same and the nature of the injuries Rs.70,000/- is awarded under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 95,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs.4,47,500/-
c.

Towards loss of income during Rs. 48,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 7,20,000/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 60,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 13,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 80,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 70,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Ashoka Leyland vehicle bearing Sanoop vs Subramanian on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100355010/
7 No.TN-30-BP-7120 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

entities.text: Ashoka Leyland vehicle bearing Sanoop vs Subramanian
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.15,33,500/-
(Rupees Fifteen lakhs thirty three thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
